MODELS AND NODES USED IN THIS WORKFLOW

 Load Diffusion Model

Download minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors19.5 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/h3

Create the h3 folder if it does not exist. This is the Reference to Video version of MiniMax H3 (ref2va), the one that can look at pictures and videos you give it.

READ LICENSE More versions 

 Load CLIP

Download qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors14.6 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/text_encoders

Qwen3-VL 32B reads your prompt AND looks at your pictures and video. It works on any recent NVIDIA card, not only the newest.

 Load VAE (video and sound)

Download minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors2.6 GB  

Download minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors577 MB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/vae

 The int8 video VAE is about twice as fast as the older fp16 one and looks the same. The fp16 one from earlier episodes still works if you already have it.

 LoRAs (in LoRA Loader Pixaroma)

The speed LoRA (DMAD 4-step, by Kijai): 4 steps instead of 20, same look.

Download minimax_h3_DMAD_4step_full_lora_avg_rank_39_bf16.safetensors350 MB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/loras/h3

Create the h3 folder inside loras if it does not exist.

 ModelPatchLoader (the H3 pose ControlNet)

Download minimax_h3_fun_controlnet_union_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors2.14 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/model_patches

 The pose readers

Download sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors1.79 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/checkpoints

Download rt_detr_v4-x-hgnet_fp16.safetensors118 MB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models

 After placing the files, restart ComfyUI or refresh model lists using the R shortcut.

 Nodes Installed from Manager

  • Pixaroma, version 1.4.183 or newer. A node shows red or missing? Update Pixaroma.

Which version is the newest? The Latest Pixaroma version button shows it and what is new in it. The help page has the update steps for every kind of install.

Latest Pixaroma version How to update Pixaroma 

 Something missing?

Each button opens a short video that shows the fix, with the steps written under it.

Red or missing nodes A model file is missing Buttons missing after an update 

 Resources

Join Discord  Pixaroma YouTube Channel  Ask for help

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Your character in a NEW place, doing exactly the moves of your video. Only the body pose comes from the video: the person, the clothes, the place and the light all come from your picture and your prompt. To keep the original place, use workflow 2 (Character Swap) instead.

 Steps

  1. 1. Pick how many seconds.
  2. 2. Pick the size.
  3. 3. Load the video with the moves: one person, the whole body or knees-up in view.
  4. 4. Load your character (a character sheet works best).
  5. 5. In Find and Replace, fill the 3 boxes: your character, what they do, the new place.
  6. Press Run.

 The 3 boxes

  • [CHARACTER]: your character the way the sheet shows them: young woman with shoulder-length black hair in a red leather jacket, a white t-shirt, blue jeans and white sneakers.
  • [WHAT THEY DO]: the moves of your video in a few words: does slow tai chi moves, dances energetically.
  • [NEW PLACE]: where it happens: a quiet temple courtyard with red wooden pillars and stone lanterns at sunrise, the grey surface of the moon with the black starry sky behind.

 Good to know

  • The first Run also loads the pose readers; reading the pose takes about a minute for 5 seconds.
  • The stick-figure video is saved too: if a move comes out wrong, check that the pose was read well there.
  • Keeping the ORIGINAL place and changing only the person was tested too (a mask around the person): the character came out dark and pasted on, so this workflow always makes a new place. To keep the place, use workflow 2 (Character Swap).
  • HANDS: use a clip where the hands are SHARP. Fast moves that are already blurred in your video come out smeared, and gloves, metal gauntlets or robot hands lose their fingers (tested: more steps, no speed LoRA and a softer pose did not fix it). Bare hands and slower moves (tai chi, a dance) came out with clean fingers.
  • The LAST half-second of a clip is the weakest: at 4 steps a raised hand there merged its fingers; 8 steps (the default here) fixed it. Tested and NOT the cause: kitchen attention.
  • Try another seed for another take.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Nodes look different from the video 

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"How to Use","icon":"to-do","color":"#2a9d8f"}}

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (MiniMax H3 ref2va) - MiniMax H3, the video model. This is its Reference to Video version: besides your prompt it can look at pictures and at a video you give it.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL, reads prompt and pictures) - Qwen3-VL 32B: reads your prompt and looks at your picture.
  • Load VAE (video) - Turns the finished render into video frames, and your video into the model's own format.
  • Load VAE (sound) - Turns sound into the model's format and back.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma (speed) - Holds the DMAD 4-step speed LoRA, here at 0.7 with 8 steps: in the tests the hands came out cleaner than at 1.0 with 4 steps (no merged fingers), for about 10 seconds more.
  • ModelPatchLoader (H3 pose ControlNet) - The H3 ControlNet: lets H3 follow a stick-figure video, so your character does exactly the moves of your video.
  • Load Diffusion Model (RT-DETR, finds the person) - A small detector that finds where the person is in each frame.
  • Load Checkpoint (SDPose, reads the body pose) - Reads the body, the hands and the face of the person and turns them into points.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Duration Pixaroma (1. how many seconds) - How many seconds to use from your video, turned into the frame count H3 accepts.
  • Sizes Pixaroma (2. video size) - The size of the new video. 704 x 1280 is the default: in the tests (a knight in armour) it gave a clearly finer face, armour and place than 480 (2 seeds and a full-body dance). 480 x 864 = a fast preview. The next size up, 768 x 1344, put a helmet on the knight that is not on the sheet. The Portrait / Landscape switch turns it on its side. Every size here is a multiple of 32, which H3 needs.
  • Load Video Pixaroma (3. the moves) - The video that gives the MOVES. Only the body pose is taken from it: the person, the clothes and the place all change. Its sound goes to the saved video.
  • Load Image Mini Pixaroma (4. your character) - Your character, best a character sheet (workflow 1) on a plain background.
  • Prompt Pixaroma (the prompt, leave it) - The prompt that tells H3 what to make. Leave it as it is: the words in [BRACKETS] are filled in from the Find and Replace node above.
  • Find and Replace Pixaroma (5. your character, what they do, the new place) - Your 3 boxes: [CHARACTER] = your character as the sheet shows them, [WHAT THEY DO] = the moves of your video in a few words (dances energetically, does slow tai chi moves), [NEW PLACE] = where it happens. They fill the prompt below.
  • Seed Pixaroma (6. random or fixed) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same result every Run, R (random) a new one each Run.

 Working in the background

Teal. They run by themselves: they make the steps faster, hand memory back, lock the real sound into the render or guide the moves. The line next to each one says if there is anything worth changing.

  • MiniMaxH3SigmaShift (12 / 3 for the speed LoRA) - The noise schedule for the speed LoRA: 12 for the picture, 3 for the sound. Leave it as it is.
  • MiniMaxH3FunControlNetApply (follow the stick figure) - Makes H3 follow the stick-figure video. strength 1 follows the moves closely; lower it (0.7) to give the character more freedom.
  • Model Attention Backend (faster steps) - Picks the attention maths. comfy kitchen attention makes each step about 1.7 times faster on NVIDIA and AMD cards with the same look (measured). If you get an error with it, pick pytorch attention.
  • Free VRAM Pixaroma (before the decode) - Hands the graphics card's memory back between the render and the video decode, so the decode fits on smaller cards.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • RTDETR_detect (find the person) - A small detector that finds where the person is in each frame, so the pose reader looks in the right place.
  • SDPoseKeypointExtractor (read the pose) - Reads the body, the hands and the face of the person in every frame and turns them into points.
  • SDPoseDrawKeypoints (draw the stick figure) - Draws those points as a coloured stick figure, frame by frame: the video H3 follows.
  • MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo (prompt + your character) - Builds the empty video at your size and length, and reads the prompt together with your character picture (<Picture 1> in the prompt).
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt. H3 runs at CFG 1 here, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler still needs one plugged in.
  • KSampler (8 steps) - The render: 8 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple. With the speed LoRA at 0.7, 8 steps drew cleaner hands than 4 in the tests.
  • VAE Decode (render to video frames) - Turns the finished render into video frames.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Video Pixaroma (the stick figure) - Saves the stick-figure video: what H3 follows. Handy to check that the pose was read well.
  • Save Video Pixaroma (your character, new place) - Saves the new video as MP4 into ComfyUI/output/Motion Transfer with the sound of your video.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Nodes Info","icon":"node-v5","color":"#3d7cc9"}}

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the time grows with the size and with the seconds.

Size5 seconds
704 x 1280, 8 stepsabout 2 min (101 s; the first Run after a start 176 s)
480 x 864about 1.5 min (91 s)

Times are with comfy kitchen attention (the default here). With pytorch attention the render part takes about 1.7 times as long.

About a minute of that is reading the pose.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models (about 20 GB for H3 and 15 GB for its text encoder), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.

 On a smaller card

Start with the smallest size and 5 seconds. The Free VRAM node already hands memory back before the video decode. A clip that is too big for the card gets very slow long before it stops working.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
